statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail sits in the low band because CME equity futures are still halted and the last observed tape was orderly, while Stress stays high on the pre-FOMC rates and energy backdrop and on a weekend that added both a fatal Strait of Hormuz strike and a Nasdaq-specific debate over the pace of AI development.
recommendation: Tail remains below the caution threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. One narrow window is flagged: 21:00-02:00 UTC around the Globex weekend reopen, where two days of unpriced Gulf and AI-sector headlines meet thin liquidity and the mapped state there is WATCH.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closed and orderly into a hawkish Fed week, with a fatal Hormuz strike and an AI-pacing debate framing the Sunday reopen
body: CME equity futures remain shut until 22:00 UTC, so no live NQ price path exists at assessment time. The last observed tape is Friday's: the Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,368.44, up 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51-29,473.12 range and about 105 points below the session high, so the index was not pinned at an extreme, while VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84. That structure is orderly and retracement-friendly, which keeps Tail in the low band. The backdrop is tighter than the tape suggests. Treasury yields sit at 4.95% on the 10-year, 4.56% on the 2-year and 5.37% on the 30-year; WTI is near $100.05 after a roughly 9.7% weekly gain, with Brent near $104.61; and markets price roughly an 86% chance of a 25 basis point hike at Wednesday's FOMC under Chair Kevin Warsh, with the press conference half an hour later. Equities near record highs with VIX under 16 against that stack is a thin cushion, which is why Stress is high while Tail is not. Two separate unpriced stacks now sit between this assessment and the reopen. The first is the Gulf: an Iranian commercial vessel was struck early Sunday near Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, killing one and wounding four, while Houthi forces hold the Red Sea port of Mokha and an island on the Bab el-Mandeb strait, putting a second chokepoint in play. Foreign ministers meet in Oman on Monday over an Omani shipping framework, but Bahrain has said it will not attend and Iran has tied any reopening to an end of the US blockade, so a de-escalation surprise is not the base case. The second stack is specific to this index. Anthropic's Dario Amodei published an essay on Saturday arguing that AI companies should deliberately slow the pace at which they improve model capabilities, and OpenAI's Sam Altman endorsed the idea hours later. Reporting over Sunday frames this as a direct challenge to the AI investment thesis that has led Nasdaq leadership, with public commentary ranging from a predicted double-digit drop in AI shares at Monday's open to an expectation of a quick rebound given committed multi-year AI spending. That dispersion is the point: conflicting signals widen the distribution rather than establish a one-way path, so they are scored as Stress and Confidence rather than Tail. The concentrated risk point in the coming window is therefore the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen and the two hours after it, where both stacks reprice into thin Sunday-evening liquidity; Tail enters the watch band across the flagged 21:00-02:00 UTC window as a conditional gap allowance rather than an observed move, then eases on the base case that Asian trade restores two-way flow. A second, smaller checkpoint is the 13:30 UTC US cash open, where any AI repricing meets its deepest liquidity. Monday's US calendar holds only 3-month and 6-month bill auctions at 15:30 UTC, leaving the session headline-driven with crude the main transmission channel. Shared Finviz cross-asset context collected at 19:00 UTC is fresh but partial, with its calendar section unavailable; its futures, breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections are labelled latest-session and delayed, and they show Friday's risk-on tone - NQ +0.86%, VIX -8.41%, technology and communication services sectors up around 1.1-1.3% - which is consistent with the verified Friday close but is not evidence of any live path, and it was used only as confirmation.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours were available and uniformly green with the mapped state EA_ON. Tail held flat at 6 from late Saturday through the overnight hours, then drifted up from 05:00 UTC to 17 by 15:00 UTC as the weekend ran toward the futures reopen, easing to 16 and then stepping to 18 in the final hour. Stress rose steadily from 52 to 73 as the pre-FOMC rates and energy backdrop accumulated, the dominant mode stayed normal throughout, and Confidence held near 86 before stepping down to the low 70s from 16:00 UTC as the weekend evidence gap widened.
outlookSummary: The window splits into three phases. Until 22:00 UTC the CME equity complex is closed and no price path can form, so Tail holds in the low band and rises only as a forward allowance into the reopen. The 21:00-02:00 UTC stretch around the Globex reopen is the concentrated risk point, where two unpriced stacks - Gulf shipping escalation and a Nasdaq-specific debate over slowing AI development - reprice into thin liquidity; Tail enters the watch band there as a conditional gap allowance rather than an observed move. From the Asian hours onward the base case is absorption of the gap and a return to two-way trade, with Tail decaying toward 17 through the European session and a second conditional uptick into the 13:30 UTC US cash open, where any AI-sector repricing meets its deepest liquidity. Monday's US calendar holds only routine bill auctions at 15:30 UTC, so residual risk is headline-driven, with crude the main transmission channel and the Oman meeting an unresolved checkpoint that Iranian officials have already tied to an end of the US blockade. Stress stays in the high band throughout because the underlying tension - a live hike debate, a 10-year near 5%, crude near $100 and two contested chokepoints - is unresolved before Wednesday. Confidence starts in the solid band and improves once a live tradable price path exists again.
